subject.title: fix(msteams): add timeouts to file consent upload requests

question: Which branch should own the canonical Microsoft Teams abortable-request helper and upload-timeout policy before either overlapping PR merges?
rationale: Both PRs fix distinct user paths but modify the same owner module with different transfer policies, so landing order and the permanent shared contract require coordinated maintainer intent.

options.title: Consolidate transfer-aware policy
options.body: Adopt one transfer-aware helper contract for both consent and group/channel SharePoint uploads, rebase the other branch onto it, and require exact-head transport proof before merge.

options.title: Land one then reconcile
options.body: Choose one PR to land first and require the second to rebase, remove duplicate helper changes, and justify any remaining policy difference.

options.title: Pause both branches
options.body: Hold both PRs until a Microsoft Teams owner defines the shared timeout contract and proof expectations.

recommendation.title: Consolidate transfer-aware policy
recommendation.body: Adopt one transfer-aware helper contract for both consent and group/channel SharePoint uploads, rebase the other branch onto it, and require exact-head transport proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history connects this owner to the file-consent path and shared timeout module affected by both PRs.
